title.value: Halting Time is Predictable for Large Models: A Universality Property and Average-case Analysis
title.justification: The title captures the main focus of the paper, which is to discuss the predictability of halting time for large models due to a universality property and average-case analysis.
title.quote: Halting Time is Predictable for Large Models: A Universality Property and Average-case Analysis

extractions.description: This paper explores the predictability of halting time for large-scale problems trained with first-order methods. It introduces a universality property indicating that halting time is independent of the probability distribution of inputs for certain models. It provides explicit average-case convergence rates and suggests this property holds for a general class of algorithms.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the theoretical aspects of optimization algorithms for large-scale models and does not directly deal with eco-responsible themes such as climate science or natural systems protection.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we analyze the halting time and develop the first explicit average-case analysis for first-order methods on quadratic objectives.

secondary_categories.justification: The content focuses on the theoretical analysis of optimization algorithms which do not concern eco-responsible subjects.
secondary_categories.quote: Yet, average-case analysis is rarely used in op- timization because the complexity of algorithms is assumed to depend on the specific probability dis- tribution of the inputs.
